title: A system on the base agrees with the completion of a proper pushforward up to a power of the exceptional ideal
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal J,\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals, $V=Y\setminus V(\mathcal K)$ ($V(\mathcal K)$ the closed set where $\mathcal K$ is not the unit ideal) and $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] such that $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism. Put $\mathcal I=f^{-1}\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal O_X$. Let $(\mathcal G_n)$ be an object of $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] and $\beta:(f^*\mathcal G_n)\to\mathcal F^\wedge$ an isomorphism in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-pullback]. Then $f_*\mathcal F$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module, and there are a morphism $\alpha:(\mathcal G_n)\to(f_*\mathcal F)^\wedge$ in $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$ and an integer $t\ge1$ such that the kernel and the cokernel of $\alpha$, taken in the abelian category $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian], are annihilated by $\mathcal K^t$ (all their terms are killed by $\mathcal K^t$).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull), with 'kernel and cokernel annihilated by a power of K' in the sense of Remark 0888 (remark-inverse-systems-kernel-cokernel-annihilated-by), whose equivalent conditions (1)-(3) give the annihilation of the kernel and cokernel objects (affine-locally the finite modules Ker(alpha_U), Coker(alpha_U) of Lemma 087W)

proof.text: (Setting.) $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence of finite type and quasi-compact; as $Y$ is Noetherian, $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] with quasi-compact underlying space, i.e. Noetherian. $\mathcal I=f^{-1}\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal O_X=\mathcal J\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals with $\mathcal I^n=\mathcal J^n\mathcal O_X$ for all $n$, and $f^*(\mathcal G/\mathcal J^n\mathcal G)\cong f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^nf^*\mathcal G$ naturally for quasi-coherent $\mathcal G$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1)-(3). So $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, $\mathcal F^\wedge=(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)_n$ and the system $(f^*\mathcal G_n)$ (an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-pullback] (1)) make sense [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For an open $W\subseteq Y$, $f_W:f^{-1}(W)\to W$ is again proper (base change of $f$ along the open immersion $W\to Y$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b)), and all hypotheses restrict to $W$: $f_W$ is an isomorphism over $V\cap W=W\setminus V(\mathcal K|_W)$, and $\beta|_{f^{-1}W}$ is an isomorphism $(f_W^*(\mathcal G_n|_W))\to(\mathcal F|_{f^{-1}W})^\wedge$ (restriction to an open is the pullback along the open immersion, [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-pullback] (2)).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull, line 7025), setting; the restriction to opens is implicit in 'we may assume Y affine'

proof.text: (Coherence of $f_*\mathcal F$.) $Y$ is locally Noetherian and $f$ proper, so for every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ the $\mathcal O_Y$-module $f_*\mathcal E=R^0f_*\mathcal E$ is coherent [lem-pc-coherent-hi]; in particular $f_*\mathcal F$ and $f_*(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ are coherent ($\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ is coherent, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] (2)), and $(f_*\mathcal F)^\wedge$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$. If $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine, $\Gamma(Y,f_*\mathcal E)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal E)$ by definition of $f_*$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull, line 7025), first sentence: Proposition 02O5 (proposition-proper-pushforward-coherent)

proof.text: (The maps $\gamma_n$ and $\kappa_n$.) Let $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^*$ be the unit of the adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ on modules [def-pc-module-pullback], and put $\gamma_n=f_*(\beta_n)\circ\eta_{\mathcal G_n}:\mathcal G_n\to f_*f^*\mathcal G_n\to f_*(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$. By naturality of $\eta$ and since $\beta$ commutes with the transition maps, the $\gamma_n$ commute with the transition maps $\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_n$ and $f_*(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F)\to f_*(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$. The map $f_*(\pi_n):f_*\mathcal F\to f_*(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ ($\pi_n$ the quotient map) kills $\mathcal J^nf_*\mathcal F$, because $\mathcal J^n$ acts on $f_*(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ through $f^\sharp$, i.e. through $\mathcal J^n\mathcal O_X=\mathcal I^n$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (2), which kills $\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$; so it induces $\kappa_n:f_*\mathcal F/\mathcal J^nf_*\mathcal F\to f_*(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$, compatible with the transition maps. All of this commutes with restriction to opens $W\subseteq Y$ (the pushforward, the pullback and the unit are computed locally over $Y$), giving the $\gamma_n,\kappa_n$ of $f_W$. Claim (proved in the next two steps): there is exactly one morphism $\alpha:(\mathcal G_n)\to(f_*\mathcal F)^\wedge$ of $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$ with $\kappa_n\circ\alpha_n=\gamma_n$ for all $n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull, line 7025), the compositions gamma_n and the claim

proof.text: (The claim for $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ affine.) Let $J=\mathcal J(Y)$, $B^\wedge$ the $J$-adic completion, $M=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=\Gamma(Y,f_*\mathcal F)$, $M_n=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)=\Gamma(Y,f_*(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F))$, $N_n=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal G_n)$ and $N=\varprojlim_nN_n$. As $f_*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent (Step 2), $\Gamma(Y,f_*\mathcal F/\mathcal J^nf_*\mathcal F)=M/J^nM$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2), and $\Gamma(\kappa_n)$ is the map $\theta_n:M/J^nM\to M_n$ induced by $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$. By the theorem on formal functions [lem-weil-pbc-theorem-formal-functions] ($p=0$, $A=B$, $I=J$; $\mathcal I=J\mathcal O_X$ by Step 1) $\psi=\varprojlim\theta_n:M^\wedge=\varprojlim M/J^nM\to\varprojlim M_n$ is bijective, and it is $B^\wedge$-linear (componentwise). Let $E:\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)\to\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}(B^\wedge)$, $(\mathcal H_n)\mapsto\varprojlim\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H_n)$, be the equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2): $E((\mathcal G_n))=N$, with surjective projections $p_n:N\to N_n$ (ibid. (1)), and $E((f_*\mathcal F)^\wedge)=M^\wedge$, with projections $\mathrm{pr}_n:M^\wedge\to M/J^nM$. Since all sheaves involved are quasi-coherent on the affine $Y$, a map between them is determined by its effect on global sections [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3); so a morphism $\alpha$ with $E(\alpha)=\varphi$ satisfies $\kappa_n\circ\alpha_n=\gamma_n$ iff $\theta_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_n\circ\varphi=\Gamma(\gamma_n)\circ p_n$ for all $n$ (using $\Gamma(\alpha_n)\circ p_n=\mathrm{pr}_n\circ\varphi$ and the surjectivity of $p_n$), i.e. iff $\psi\circ\varphi=\varprojlim_n\Gamma(\gamma_n)$ (the $n$-th component of $\psi$ is $\theta_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_n$). As $\psi$ is bijective there is exactly one such $\varphi$, namely $\varphi=\psi^{-1}\circ\varprojlim_n\Gamma(\gamma_n):N\to M^\wedge$, which is $B^\wedge$-linear; as $E$ is an equivalence (bijective on morphisms) there is exactly one $\alpha$, and $E(\alpha)=\varphi$. We write $\varphi=\alpha_Y$ (the notation of [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-annihilated-by-power]).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull, line 7025), paragraph 'Because of the uniqueness we may assume that Y = Spec(B) is affine ...': Lemma 02OB (lemma-ML-cohomology-powers-ideal), Theorem 02OC (theorem-formal-functions) and Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine)

proof.text: (Globalization, and reduction of the annihilation to affine $Y$.) For every affine open $W\subseteq Y$ the previous step, applied to $f_W$ (Step 1), gives a unique $\alpha^W$ on $W$ with $\kappa_n|_W\circ\alpha^W_n=\gamma_n|_W$. For affine opens $W'\subseteq W$, $\alpha^W|_{W'}$ satisfies the defining equations on $W'$ (Step 3: everything commutes with restriction, and $(f_*\mathcal F)^\wedge|_{W'}=((f_{W'})_*\mathcal F|_{f^{-1}W'})^\wedge$ by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-pullback] (2)), so $\alpha^W|_{W'}=\alpha^{W'}$. As the affine opens form a basis of $Y$ stable under the passage to smaller affine opens of intersections, the sheaf maps $\alpha^W_n$ glue to $\mathcal O_Y$-linear $\alpha_n:\mathcal G_n\to f_*\mathcal F/\mathcal J^nf_*\mathcal F$ (morphisms of sheaves glue); the identities $\kappa_n\circ\alpha_n=\gamma_n$ and the compatibility with the transition maps hold since they hold on every affine $W$. Any $\alpha'$ with $\kappa_n\circ\alpha'_n=\gamma_n$ restricts on each affine $W$ to $\alpha^W$, so $\alpha'=\alpha$: the claim of Step 3 holds. Now choose a finite covering $Y=W_1\cup\dots\cup W_r$ by affine opens ($Y$ is Noetherian). By [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-annihilated-by-power], (3)$\Rightarrow$(4), it suffices to show: for each $i$ there is $t_i\ge1$ with $\mathcal K(W_i)^{t_i}$ killing $\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_{W_i})$ and $\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha_{W_i})$ (then take $t=\max t_i$); here $\alpha_{W_i}$ is the map $\varphi$ of Step 4 for $f_{W_i}$, as $\alpha|_{W_i}=\alpha^{W_i}$. So from now on $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine, $J=\mathcal J(Y)$, $K=\mathcal K(Y)$, and we must show that $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ are killed by a power of $K$.

proof.text: (Base change to the completion: the new situation.) Let $B'=B^\wedge$ be the $J$-adic completion; $B'$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $JB'$-adically complete [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] (1), the map $B\to B'$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], and $B/J^n\to B'/J^nB'$ is an isomorphism for every $n$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power]. Put $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}B'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $X'=X\times_YY'$ with projections $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$ [def-pc-base-change]. Then $f'$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b) and $Y'$, $X'$ are Noetherian (Step 1 for $f'$). Let $\mathcal J'=\mathcal J\mathcal O_{Y'}=(JB')^\sim$, $\mathcal K'=\mathcal K\mathcal O_{Y'}=(KB')^\sim$ and $\mathcal I'=\mathcal J'\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X'}$ (on affine opens all three are generated by the images of $J$, $K$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1)). $V'=g^{-1}(V)$ equals $Y'\setminus V(\mathcal K')$ ($B\to B'$ induces local homomorphisms of the local rings, so $\mathcal K'_{y'}$ is the unit ideal iff $\mathcal K_{g(y')}$ is), and $f'^{-1}(V')=f^{-1}(V)\times_VV'\to V'$ is the base change of the isomorphism $f^{-1}(V)\to V$, hence an isomorphism. Put $\mathcal G'_n=g^*\mathcal G_n$, an object $(\mathcal G'_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(Y',\mathcal J')$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-pullback] (1), and $\mathcal F'=g'^*\mathcal F$, coherent (quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] (3), on a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]). With $(fg')^*\cong(gf')^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], $\beta'$ is the composite isomorphism $(f'^*\mathcal G'_n)\cong(g'^*f^*\mathcal G_n)\xrightarrow{g'^*\beta}g'^*(\mathcal F^\wedge)\cong\mathcal F'^\wedge$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X',\mathcal I')$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-pullback] (1),(2). So the hypotheses of the lemma hold for $(Y',\mathcal J',\mathcal K',f',(\mathcal G'_n),\mathcal F',\beta')$; let $\gamma'_n,\kappa'_n,\alpha',\varphi'=\alpha'_{Y'}$ be the data of Steps 3-4 for it (the completion of $B'$ along $JB'$ is $B'$ itself).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull, line 7025), paragraph 'Set Y' = Spec(B^) and X' = Y' x_Y X': Algebra Lemma 00MB (algebra-lemma-completion-flat), More on Algebra Lemma 05EC (more-algebra-lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence)

proof.text: (Base change does not change $\varphi$.) Every $\mathcal O_Y$-module killed by $\mathcal J^n$ that is quasi-coherent, $\mathcal P=\widetilde P$, satisfies $\Gamma(Y',g^*\mathcal P)=B'\otimes_BP=(B'/J^nB')\otimes_{B/J^n}P=P$ [lem-weil-pbc-associated-module-pullback], [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power]. Hence $N'_n=\Gamma(Y',\mathcal G'_n)=N_n$ and $N'=\varprojlim N'_n=N$. By flat base change for the quasi-compact separated $f$ and the flat $g$ [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] (case $i=0$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $S'=\operatorname{Spec}B'$), $s\otimes b\mapsto b\cdot g'^*s$ gives $M'=\Gamma(X',\mathcal F')=M\otimes_BB'$ and $M'_n=\Gamma(X',g'^*(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F))=M_n\otimes_BB'=M_n$, where $g'^*(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)=\mathcal F'/\mathcal I'^n\mathcal F'$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (3); so $M'/J^nM'=M/J^nM$ and $M'^\wedge=M^\wedge$, and under these identifications $\theta'_n=\theta_n$, $\psi'=\psi$. On global sections $\Gamma(\gamma_n)$ sends $x\in N_n$ to $\beta_n(f^*x)$ and $\Gamma(\gamma'_n)$ sends $b\otimes x$ to $b\cdot\beta'_n(f'^*g^*x)=b\cdot g'^*(\beta_n(f^*x))$ (definition of $\beta'$ in Step 6 and of the unit, [def-pc-module-pullback]); so $\Gamma(\gamma'_n)=\Gamma(\gamma_n)$ under the identifications, and $\varphi'=\psi'^{-1}\circ\varprojlim\Gamma(\gamma'_n)=\varphi$ as maps $N\to M^\wedge$. The ideal $\mathcal K'(Y')=KB'$ satisfies $(KB')^t=K^tB'$, and $K^tB'$ kills a $B'$-module iff $K^t$ does. Therefore it suffices to show that $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi'$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi'$ are killed by a power of $\mathcal K'(Y')$, i.e. we may assume that $B$ is $J$-adically complete.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull, line 7025), 'Hence f'_*F', resp. f'_*(f')^*G'_n is the pullback of f_*F, resp. f_*f^*G_n to Y' by Lemma 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology). The uniqueness of our construction shows the pullback of alpha to Y' is the corresponding map alpha' ... Thus we may assume B is complete with respect to J'; the comparison is made here on the modules N, M^ directly instead of on the terms alpha_n (agent's rewording of the same argument)

proof.text: (Complete case: algebraizing $(\mathcal G'_n)$ and $\beta'$.) Now $B'$ is Noetherian and $JB'$-adically complete, so $B'\to B'^\wedge$ is bijective [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. $N'$ is a finitely generated $B'$-module [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (1); $\mathcal G'=\widetilde{N'}$ is coherent ([lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] (a), [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]) with $\Gamma(Y',\mathcal G'/\mathcal J'^n\mathcal G')=N'/J^nN'$ ([lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2), [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (2)), so $\mathcal G'^\wedge$ is the image of $N'$ under the quasi-inverse of $E$ in [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2), and there is an isomorphism $\iota:\mathcal G'^\wedge\to(\mathcal G'_n)$ in $\mathit{Coh}(Y',\mathcal J')$ with $E(\iota)=\mathrm{id}_{N'}$. $f'^*\mathcal G'$ is coherent (as for $\mathcal F'$ in Step 6). The composite $(f'^*\mathcal G')^\wedge\cong f'^*(\mathcal G'^\wedge)\xrightarrow{f'^*\iota}(f'^*\mathcal G'_n)\xrightarrow{\beta'}\mathcal F'^\wedge$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-pullback] (1),(2) is an isomorphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X',\mathcal I')$; since the completion functor is fully faithful for the proper $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}B'$ over the complete Noetherian $B'$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-completion-fully-faithful-proper], it is $b^\wedge$ for a unique $\mathcal O_{X'}$-linear $b:f'^*\mathcal G'\to\mathcal F'$, and $b$ is an isomorphism (the inverse isomorphism is $b_1^\wedge$ for some $b_1$, and $(b_1b)^\wedge=\mathrm{id}$, $(bb_1)^\wedge=\mathrm{id}$ give $b_1b=\mathrm{id}$, $bb_1=\mathrm{id}$ by faithfulness).

proof.text: (Complete case: $\alpha'$ is the completion of an adjunction map.) Let $c:\mathcal G'\to f'_*f'^*\mathcal G'$ be the unit [def-pc-module-pullback] and $c'=f'_*(b)\circ c:\mathcal G'\to f'_*\mathcal F'$, a map of coherent $\mathcal O_{Y'}$-modules (Step 2). Put $\alpha''=c'^\wedge\circ\iota^{-1}:(\mathcal G'_n)\to(f'_*\mathcal F')^\wedge$. With $q_n:\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G'/\mathcal J'^n\mathcal G'$ and the identification $f'^*(\mathcal G'/\mathcal J'^n\mathcal G')=f'^*\mathcal G'/\mathcal I'^nf'^*\mathcal G'$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (3), under which $\beta'_n\circ f'^*(\iota_n)=b\bmod\mathcal I'^n$ (Step 8), naturality of the unit gives $\gamma'_n\circ\iota_n\circ q_n=f'_*(\beta'_n\circ f'^*\iota_n)\circ\eta_{\mathcal G'/\mathcal J'^n}\circ q_n=f'_*((b\bmod\mathcal I'^n)\circ f'^*q_n)\circ c=f'_*(\pi'_n\circ b)\circ c=f'_*(\pi'_n)\circ c'=\kappa'_n\circ(c'\bmod\mathcal J'^n)\circ q_n$; as $q_n$ is an epimorphism, $\kappa'_n\circ\alpha''_n=\gamma'_n$ for all $n$, so $\alpha''=\alpha'$ by the uniqueness of Steps 4-5. The components of $\alpha''$ are $\alpha''_n=(c'\bmod\mathcal J'^n)\circ\iota_n^{-1}$, with $\iota_n$ isomorphisms, so $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha'_n\cong\operatorname{Ker}(c'\bmod\mathcal J'^n)$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\alpha'_n\cong\operatorname{Coker}(c'\bmod\mathcal J'^n)$. Since $f'_*(b)$ is an isomorphism, $\operatorname{Ker}c'\cong\operatorname{Ker}c$ and $\operatorname{Coker}c'\cong\operatorname{Coker}c$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull, line 7025), last paragraph: 'alpha is the completion functor applied to G -> f_*f^*G = f_*F. Hence we are trying to verify that the kernel and cokernel of the adjunction map c are annihilated by a power of K'

proof.text: (Complete case: the adjunction map is an isomorphism over $V'$.) The restriction of $c$ to $V'$ is the unit of $f'^*\dashv f'_*$ for $f'_{V'}:f'^{-1}(V')\to V'$ (pushforward, pullback and unit are computed locally over $Y'$ [def-pc-module-pullback]); as $f'_{V'}$ is an isomorphism (Step 6), $f'_{V'*}$ and $f'^*_{V'}$ are mutually inverse equivalences and this unit is an isomorphism. So $\operatorname{Ker}c$ and $\operatorname{Coker}c$, coherent $\mathcal O_{Y'}$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] (1) (as $f'_*f'^*\mathcal G'$ is coherent, Step 2), have zero stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] at every point of $V'$ (stalks of kernels and cokernels are kernels and cokernels of stalks), i.e. $\operatorname{Supp}\subseteq Y'\setminus V'=V(\mathcal K')$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] (2). As $Y'$ is Noetherian, there is $s\ge1$ with $\mathcal K'^s\operatorname{Ker}c=0$ and $\mathcal K'^s\operatorname{Coker}c=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-support-power-ideal-kills].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull, line 7025), last paragraph: 'since the restriction f|_{f^{-1}(V)} is an isomorphism we see that c|_V is an isomorphism. Thus Ker(c) and Coker(c) are supported on V(K) hence are annihilated by a power of K (Lemma 01Y9, lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf)'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) On the affine $Y'$ take global sections: $u=\Gamma(Y',c'):P=N'\to Q=M'$ is $B'$-linear with $\operatorname{Ker}u=\Gamma(\operatorname{Ker}c')$, $\operatorname{Coker}u=\Gamma(\operatorname{Coker}c')$ (quasi-coherent modules on an affine scheme, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (3)), killed by $(KB')^s$ (Steps 9-10, [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2)). By the commutative algebra fact of [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-annihilated-by-power] applied to $0\to\operatorname{Ker}u\to P\xrightarrow{u}Q\to\operatorname{Coker}u\to0$ and $J^nB'$, the kernel and cokernel of $u\bmod J^n:P/J^nP\to Q/J^nQ$, which are the global sections of $\operatorname{Ker}(c'\bmod\mathcal J'^n)$ and $\operatorname{Coker}(c'\bmod\mathcal J'^n)$, are killed by $(KB')^{2s}$ for every $n$; hence (sections over the affine $Y'$ determine these quasi-coherent sheaves and their products with $\mathcal K'^{2s}$, same references) $\mathcal K'^{2s}$ kills $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha'_n$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\alpha'_n$ for all $n$ (Step 9). This is condition (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-annihilated-by-power] for $\alpha'$ on $Y'$, so by (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) there (with $U=Y'$) $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi'$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi'$ are killed by a power of $KB'$. By Step 7, $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ are killed by a power of $K$, and by Step 5 there is $t\ge1$ such that the kernel and cokernel of $\alpha$ in the abelian category $\mathit{Coh}(Y,\mathcal J)$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] are annihilated by $\mathcal K^t$.
